-- EP-488 v50 / G5: Degree-3 is strict local minimum
-- Claim: If deg_B(a) = 3, every neighbor of a in the n-LCM graph is > a.
-- Proof: potential smaller neighbors would be 2a/3, 3a/4, 3a/5, or 4a/5.
-- All are < q/2 when a < 3q/5, so none can lie in C ⊂ (q/2, q].
--
-- Simplified target: show each of the four expressions is < q/2 under a < 3q/5.

import Mathlib.Tactic

/-- If a < 3q/5, then 2a/3 < 2q/5 < q/2. -/
theorem smaller_neighbor_2a_3_below_q_2
    {q a : ℕ}
    (hq : 0 < q)
    (ha : 5 * a < 3 * q)  -- a < 3q/5
    (hdiv : 3 ∣ a) :
    2 * (2 * a / 3) < q := by
  sorry

/-- If a < 3q/5, then 3a/4 < 9q/20 < q/2. -/
theorem smaller_neighbor_3a_4_below_q_2
    {q a : ℕ}
    (hq : 0 < q)
    (ha : 5 * a < 3 * q)
    (hdiv : 4 ∣ a) :
    2 * (3 * a / 4) < q := by
  sorry

/-- If a < 3q/5, then 4a/5 < 12q/25 < q/2. -/
theorem smaller_neighbor_4a_5_below_q_2
    {q a : ℕ}
    (hq : 0 < q)
    (ha : 5 * a < 3 * q)
    (hdiv : 5 ∣ a) :
    2 * (4 * a / 5) < q := by
  sorry
